items.title: Jefferies picks 5 financial stocks with upside of up to 25%. How many do you have?
items.description: Jefferies has identified five financial companies with market capitalisation of around or above $5 billion that could deliver 25% CAGR in operating profit over the next three years, supported by healthy revenue growth and economies of scale. The foreign brokerage has rated all five as Buys, expecting strong earnings compounding to drive investor returns despite their relatively higher valuations.

items.title: NSE IPO: Market dominance vs regulatory risks; what investors should know from the RHP
items.description: In its red herring prospectus (RHP), NSE has highlighted its market leadership, scale, profitability, technology infrastructure and cash generation as key strengths. The exchange, however, has also flagged several risks, including dependence on trading volumes, regulatory changes and increased scrutiny.

items.title: Global funds sour on India stocks as some cut allocation to zero
items.description: Global investors are reducing Indian equity exposure due to a lack of AI investment themes. Foreign portfolio ownership has fallen to a seventeen-year low as funds exit the market. India now ranks as the least-favored market in Asia according to a recent survey. Local institutions are providing support, but foreign capital remains a concern. Investors seek more durable foreign direct investments to fuel manufacturing ambitions.

items.title: Oversold markets may stage near-term rebound, say analysts
items.description: Indian equities experienced a decline on Friday, mirroring Asian markets' downward trend. Both Nifty and Sensex indices closed lower for a fifth consecutive week. Rising crude oil prices and US bond yields kept investors on edge throughout the trading session. Broader market indices also saw a dip, reflecting the overall market sentiment. Despite some recovery, the market's fear gauge, VIX, increased significantly.

items.title: Sitharaman calls AI a ‘double-edged sword’, urges soft-touch regulation and faster digital rupee push
items.description: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman highlighted artificial intelligence as a double-edged sword for financial systems. She advocated for a soft-touch regulatory framework for emerging technologies and innovation. The minister urged the Reserve Bank of India to accelerate its digital rupee pilots and capabilities. Sitharaman also dismissed pessimism regarding India's demographic dividend, emphasizing youth-led growth.

items.title: Bank deposits grow 17.8% in August, fastest in decade as FCNR-B inflows mask local mobilisation woes
items.description: Bank deposits grew 17.8% year-on-year at the end of August, the fastest pace in a decade, driven largely by a surge in FCNR-B deposits after RBI opened a special window for dollar inflows. Credit growth eased slightly to 19.1%, while banks continued to face challenges in mobilising domestic savings.

items.title: Demat 2.0 explained: Why it matters for bond market investors
items.description: In an innovative move, Sebi has rolled out Demat 2.0, a pilot scheme aimed at tokenising corporate bonds. This initiative facilitates rapid settlement and instant fund retrieval for investors. It automates interest and redemption payments through smart contracts, while atomic settlement mitigates risks by coordinating the release of bonds and payments seamlessly. Future developments will broaden this system's reach to secondary markets and individual investors.

items.title: Goldman Sachs’ India Portfolio; 10 stocks rally up to 130% in CY26
items.description: Goldman Sachs’ Indian equity portfolio, held through its global funds, declined sharply by 27% in CY26, with its value falling from Rs 9,015 crore in December 2025 to Rs 6,585 crore as of September 11, 2026. As of the June 2026 quarter, the portfolio comprised around 39 stocks, of which 18 declined by 10–40% so far in CY26. Despite the overall decline, 10 stocks delivered gains ranging from 20% to 130% during the period. CMR Green Technologies was a newly added stock to the portfolio during the June 2026 quarter. (Data Source: ACE Equity, Trendlyne)

items.title: BSE volumes ease after sharp rebound; CAS remains in focus: Nuvama
items.description: For FY27 to date, BSE’s ADPTV is around Rs 26,200 crore, while its ADPTV market share is around 35.2%. Its premium-to-notional turnover ratio is around 12.4 basis points, compared with 17.2 basis points for the industry.

items.title: Sebi proposes new CAS framework, two options for expiry-day settlement
items.description: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is set to implement crucial updates to the Closing Auction Session. A focus of these changes is on the process of derivatives settlement on expiry days. SEBI has laid out two alternatives for determining the derivatives settlement price: the first proposes a blended VWAP approach after one year, while the second keeps the current CTS VWAP process in place for the present.

items.title: PMS Tracker: East Green, Atlas Integrated Finance, Hem Securities, 7 others deliver up to 14.7% returns in August
items.description: Equity PMS strategies posted strong gains during the month, led by East Green Advisors' Quant Strategy, which emerged as the best performer with a 14.73% return for the month ended August 31, 2026.

items.title: Concurrent Gainers: 9 smallcap stocks gain for 5 days in a row
items.description: Over the five trading sessions ending September 11, the Sensex declined 2.27%, or 1,734 points, to close at 74,781, falling in four of the five sessions. Despite the broader market weakness, about 17 stocks from the BSE SmallCap index advanced in each of the five consecutive sessions from September 7 to September 11. Of these, we identified 12 stocks that gained on all five days, delivering cumulative returns ranging from 10% to 30% during the period. (Data Source: ACE Equity)
